chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام about a man whom a wild beast encounters, while the time of salat (prayer) has arrived, and he is unable to walk out of fear of the beast. He said:
"He should face the lion, perform the salat (prayer), and gesture with his head in indication while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the qiblah."

key_terms.السَّبُعُ: a wild beast threatening the person
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat (prayer) whose time has entered
key_terms.الْأَسَدَ: the lion that must be faced due to danger
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer, which is excused here due to necessity
key_terms.بِرَأْسِهِ: with his head, indicating the manner of gesture
key_terms.قَائِمٌ: while standing, as his prayer posture in this circumstance
key_terms.يُومِئُ: he gestures as a substitute for fuller prayer movements

ai.seo_question: How should someone perform salat (prayer) if a wild beast prevents him from turning toward the qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for salat (prayer) in a state of danger when a person is immobilized by fear of a wild beast. It indicates that he should pray in the way he is able, facing the threat and signaling with his head while standing, even if that prevents facing the qiblah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1336 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) about a man who encounters a wild beast, and the time for prayer has arrived, but he is unable to walk due to fear of the beast.
Imam (as) said: "He should face the lion, perform the prayer, and gesture with his head while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the Qibla."
